newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma hopes to hold talks with Karen guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Burma hopes to hold talks with Karen guerrillas.

text.p: Burma's ruling military government wants to hold a new round of peace talks with the Karen ethnic guerrilla group despite accusing the rebels of involvement in a recent bomb attack, a senior official said on Thursday.

Colonel Kyaw Win, deputy chief of intelligence, told reporters the Burmese government was ready to resume talks with the Karen National Union (KNU) -- the last major ethnic rebel group yet to sign a ceasefire agreement with Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).

"We are ready to resume negotiations. We do not have any intention of suspending the peace talks because of their involvement in the bombing," Kyaw Win told a monthly news briefing. He said talks were originally due to resume in December.
The SLORC has accused the KNU of being involved in a December 25 bombing at a Buddhist shrine in the outskirts of Rangoon. The blast killed five and wounded 17.
The KNU has denied any involvement in the bombing.
Colonel Kyaw Thein, another senior intelligence official, said at the news conference the KNU was responsible for all bomb explosions in Burma since the early 1970s.
Kyaw Win said he had just received indications from the KNU that it was ready to sit down to a new round of talks with the SLORC.
KNU officials on the Thai-Burma border told Reuters they were ready to hold new talks despite failing to reach agreement in four previous rounds of negotiations.
"We hope this year (1997) we might reach a peace agreement," a KNU official said.
Past sticking points included the SLORC's demand that the KNU give up its policy of armed struggle.
Fifteen ethnic groups have signed ceasefire agreements with the SLORC since 1989 and are cooperating in regional development activities.
